expectations.text: States that instructions to a model are not enforcement, regardless of wording or emphasis
expectations.evidence: An agent will eventually forget or bypass a rule in `CLAUDE.md` no matter how many times you capitalize it

expectations.text: Redirects away from rewording CLAUDE.md as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: replace the written instructions with Rung 1 (Control) mechanical devices

expectations.text: Recommends permission deny rules in settings.json with concrete syntax
expectations.evidence: You can block this by denying the `Edit` tool outright using real syntax: `"Edit(./src/generated/**)"`

expectations.text: Recommends a PreToolUse hook for cases that need logic rather than a pattern match
expectations.evidence: To block this reliably, you need a `PreToolUse` hook script that inspects the command with a regex

expectations.text: Explains that the deny message should say what to do instead, not merely refuse
expectations.evidence: The message must tell the agent what to do instead: Blocked: Force-push can destroy commits... Use --force-with-lease if you must rewrite

expectations.text: Recommends verifying the device actually fires rather than assuming it works
expectations.evidence: Ask the agent to edit a file in `src/generated/` and watch it get denied. Then ask it to run `git push origin main --force` and confirm it sees your exact deny message

expectations.text: Recommends committing the rules so they apply to the whole team, not just one machine
expectations.evidence: Put your deny rule and hook configuration in `.claude/settings.json` and commit it. If you put it in a local gitignored file, it only protects your machine

expectations.text: Explains why repetition and capitals do not make an instruction reliable
expectations.evidence: An agent will eventually forget or bypass a rule in `CLAUDE.md` no matter how many times you capitalize it
